intro: Continents and oceans, weather on the road, and people who move from one city to another.

el turista.nota: The feminine form is la turista.

el viajero.nota: The feminine form is la viajera.

echar de menos.nota: Extrañar is also widely used, especially in Latin America.

bloques.texto:
One common school model groups the world into **cinco continentes**; other models count them differently. There are several **océanos**: el Atlántico, el Pacífico, el Índico. Spain and Portugal share **la península** Ibérica.

Weather can change a trip: **una tormenta**, **la niebla**, **una nevada**, **una ola de calor**, **una ola de frío** and **granizo**. Spanish says **hubo** una tormenta, with **haber** in the indefinido.

People travel and move. A **turista** or **viajero** visits a place and goes home. Someone who changes city **se muda** to a new **barrio**, with their **maletas**.

Useful verbs: **irse a vivir a**, **viajar** a otro país, **adaptarse a** otra ciudad, **echar de menos** la suya, **volver a** su ciudad natal.

Figures: **la población** de una ciudad; **millones de** personas; **uno de cada diez**.

frases.es: Durante el verano, millones de turistas viajaron a la costa y al norte de la península.
frases.en: During the summer, millions of tourists travelled to the coast and to the north of the peninsula.
analisis: a la costa y al norte de la península

frases.es: Muchos se iban porque en las ciudades hacía mucho calor.
frases.en: Many left because it was very hot in the cities.

frases.es: Hoy muchos jóvenes se mudan a otras ciudades, sobre todo a Madrid y a Barcelona.
frases.en: Today many young people move to other cities, above all to Madrid and Barcelona.
analisis: sobre todo a Madrid y a Barcelona

frases.es: Algunos cruzan el océano para pasar un año estudiando; otros prefieren viajar en tren por Europa.
frases.en: Some cross the ocean to spend a year studying; others prefer to travel around Europe by train.

frases.es: Adaptarse a otra ciudad no es fácil: hay que conocer los barrios y se echa de menos a la familia.
frases.en: Adapting to another city is not easy: you have to get to know the neighbourhoods and you miss your family.

frases.es: Amal explica que, por ahora, no volvería a su ciudad natal si allí no tuviera un buen trabajo.
frases.en: Amal explains that, for now, she would not go back to her hometown if she did not have a good job there.

opciones.Hubo: Haber in the indefinido: there was.
opciones.Fue: Spanish says hubo for an event that took place.

bloques.pregunta: A person who travels to see new places for fun is…

opciones.un turista: A tourist visits places for fun.
opciones.un cocinero: A cook works in a kitchen.

bloques.pregunta: According to the text, why did many people leave the cities?

opciones.It was very hot in the cities: En las ciudades hacía mucho calor.
opciones.There was a snowfall: Snow is a distractor; the text says it was hot.
opciones.They wanted to learn languages: Learning languages is a distractor; the text gives the heat as the reason.

bloques.correcta: It was very hot in the cities

opciones.explicacion: Una ola de calor is a period of very hot weather, not a wave in the sea.

opciones.texto: a hot wave in the sea
opciones.explicacion: Ola de calor is the set phrase for a heatwave.
Ola is a wave. Hola is hello.

bloques.pregunta: Complete: it is hard to adapt to another city.

opciones.a: Adaptarse a means to adapt to, so a is the right preposition.

bloques.frase: La mayoría no volvería a su ciudad natal
bloques.traduccion: Most would not go back to their hometown.

bloques.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about travel: why people move to another city, and the experience of someone you know.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud what you would miss most if you had to live in another city, or what you do miss.
